docs/architecture.md:97:`tools/reference-player.ts` serves a separate loopback-only original SWF viewer with development dependency Ruffle 0.7.1. It shares the SWF decompressor, serves WASM with the correct MIME type, and accepts a browser-local file or explicit `BT3_SWF_FILE`. `reference-browser.ts` owns a headless Chrome/CDP instance with the stack size this movie needs; `reference-input.ts` uses Node Playwright for native coordinate input and stage captures. Ruffle is never imported by `src` or included in the Next.js output. The optional original-runtime smoke test is enabled with `BT3_REFERENCE=1`; it complements simulation tests rather than establishing whole-game parity.
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    name: Rules, build and mock browser
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 35
    env:
      NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.9
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun run check
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Production build and offline browser smoke
        run: bun run test:e2e --grep 'mock|synthetic'
      - name: Retain failed browser traces
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: browser-failures
          path: test-results/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

payload.diffStr:
# Five-PR delivery stacks

The current user policy is to accumulate five dependent PRs before integrating the
batch into master. Keep each layer coherent and reviewable. PR125 is the first layer
of the current stack; do not merge it into master while fewer than five layers exist.

```text
master ← PR1 ← PR2 ← PR3 ← PR4 ← PR5
```

The bottom PR targets master. Each later PR targets the preceding layer's branch,
so its review shows that layer's change. Use `stack/<bottom-PR>-<layer>-<description>`
for intermediate branches. Preserve the legacy recreation checkpoint unchanged.

For each finalized PR, create an isolated get-green agent. Require its current-head
GitHub Actions run and the named `Rules, build and mock browser` job to complete
successfully, and address actionable review findings. Pending, missing or failed
Actions is not green. Escalate uncertain fundamental changes from the child to the
parent. Never remove assertions or suites merely to obtain green checks.

Once five layers exist and their gates pass, merge the top PR into its parent branch.
Validate the updated parent's exact head, then continue down the stack. This folds all
five changes into the bottom branch before its single final merge to master. Require
a fresh complete Actions/review gate on that combined head. If master changes during
the batch, integrate it and validate the resulting tree before the final merge. Verify
each merge result and fetched tree; do not infer completion from a queued operation.

## Vercel deployment budget

Stacking alone does not suppress preview builds. `vercel.json` sets
`git.deploymentEnabled["stack/**"]` to false, using Vercel's supported minimatch branch
rules. Intermediate pushes and merges therefore skip automatic Vercel deployments.
Unspecified branches retain their normal behavior, including master and the current
bottom integration branch. The assembled bottom branch can receive a final preview;
the one master merge can trigger the production deployment.

See [Vercel's Git configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration).
Do not add a broad true rule overlapping `stack/**`: Vercel deploys when any matching
rule enables it. A deliberate intermediate preview skip is expected; continue to
require Actions and reviews. Only the previously observed daily deployment-quota
failure is waived. Investigate other actual deployment failures, and do not retry
deployments or change billing as a response to quota exhaustion.

Validate repository configuration before pushing and inspect provider feedback to
confirm the intended skip. Configuration validity alone does not prove that Vercel
honored the branch rule. No provider account, production-branch or billing setting is
changed by this repository rule.

input.title: Skip intermediate Vercel deployments for five-PR delivery stacks
input.body:
## Summary

Stack layer2 of5, based on #125. Preserve master until five dependent PRs have passed Actions and review, then fold the layers into the bottom branch before one final master merge.

```text
master ← #125 ← this layer ← layer3 ← layer4 ← layer5
Vercel: intermediate stack/** branches disabled; final integration/master unchanged
```

Add the supported `git.deploymentEnabled` branch rule and document updated-head CI gates and top-down integration. No billing or provider-account settings change.

## Evidence

- **Before:** every intermediate branch push could trigger a preview; the handoff still required one PR at a time.
  **After:** `stack/**` is excluded from automatic deployment, and the handoff links the five-PR policy. Provider skip must be observed after push; schema validation alone does not establish it.
- JSON parses and validates against the current official Vercel schema with its declared Draft4 instance validator. Formatting and diff checks pass. No app code or dependency changes.
- Branch matching/default behavior checked against [Vercel's Git configuration](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** deployments

Intermediate PRs intentionally receive no automatic Vercel preview. Actions and review remain mandatory. Unspecified branches, including master and the bottom integration branch, retain normal deployment behavior. Hold this stack's master merge until all five layers are ready.
